description: AI tool wrappers for the My Visualizations library. Persist, search, annotate, and link React visualizations; read the originating chat thread; manage Synergy Kanban links. Backed by /api/viz/snapshots/* routes (see AI_infrastructure/routes/viz_snapshots_routes.py).

tools.name: viz_create
tools.short_description: Save an AI-rendered React visualization to the user's library
tools.description:
Persist a freshly-built React visualization (or any react/jsx source) into the 'My Visualizations' library. The snapshot is RLS-scoped to the calling user's org and tagged with the calling user as owner. Use this whenever the LLM has just rendered a dashboard/chart the user might want to revisit.

The backend stores jsx_source (verbatim), optional css_source, a list of feature flags (uses_lucide / uses_recharts / uses_tailwind) that drive the gallery badge column, and a string-array of tags. On insert the row is also stamped with org_id and owner_user_id from the JWT context, so the caller does NOT supply those.

Response includes the new id (UUID) and share_token (16-byte hex); both are stable and safe to display back to the user. The created_at / updated_at timestamps are returned ISO-8601.

USE CASES:
1. The user asks to save the dashboard the AI just rendered.
2. The user wants to bookmark a chart under a custom title before navigating away.
3. An agent is curating a multi-step analysis and wants each step's chart saved with a sequence number in the tags.

WHEN NOT TO USE:
- Reading or searching existing snapshots → use viz_search.
- Editing metadata of an existing snapshot → use viz_update.
- Linking to a Synergy session → call viz_link_synergy afterwards (or chain in same turn).

WORKFLOW:
1. AI finishes rendering a React viz (chart, table, dashboard).
2. AI strips its own wrapper boilerplate so jsx_source is just the user's component code.
3. AI calls viz_create(title=..., jsx_source=..., tags=[...], thread_id=current_thread_id, assistant_message_id=current_message_id).
4. Backend returns id + share_token.
5. AI confirms to user: 'Saved as [title] (id ...).'

BEST PRACTICES:
- Always pass thread_id and assistant_message_id so the snapshot can be navigated back to its conversation.
- Use lowercase, hyphen-friendly tags (e.g. 'q3-forecast', 'finance').
- If the JSX is large (>50KB), prefer viz_save (alias of create) so the title can double as a dedupe key for future upserts.
- Always confirm to the user before saving if jsx_source contains user PII — the snapshot is org-visible unless is_public is later set.

ERROR HANDLING:
- title or jsx_source missing → 400 with 'title and jsx_source are required'.
- org_id missing on JWT → 401.
- jsx_source > 256KB → 413 (consider external storage; not yet supported).

RELATED TOOLS:
- viz_update — patch title / tags / css / visibility after creation.
- viz_search — list snapshots with filters.
- viz_link_synergy — attach to a Synergy Kanban session after creation.

title.description: Human-readable title for the saved viz. Shown in the gallery header. Required.

jsx_source.description: The complete JSX/React source for the visualization. Required. The renderer will re-mount this verbatim when the user re-opens the snapshot.

css_source.description: Optional CSS to inject alongside the JSX (Tailwind classes should already be in the JSX; this is for custom styles).

uses_lucide.description: Set true if the JSX imports lucide-react icons. Drives the gallery badge column.

uses_recharts.description: Set true if the JSX imports recharts components.

uses_tailwind.description: Set true if the JSX relies on Tailwind utility classes (set globally so the gallery can warn if Tailwind is not loaded).

tags.description: Lowercase, hyphen-friendly tag list for gallery filtering. Example: ['finance', 'q3-forecast'].

thread_id.description: Optional sessions.threads.id this viz was rendered in. Makes the gallery tile show 'Open chat'.

assistant_message_id.description: Optional sessions.messages.id of the assistant message that produced the viz. Used by the gallery to deep-link back.

synergy_session_id.description: Optional synergy_sessions.synergy_sessions.session_id to atomically link at creation time (otherwise call viz_link_synergy afterwards).

examples.description: Simple - Save the chart we just built

parameters.title: Q3 Revenue by Region
parameters.jsx_source: function App(){const data=[{region:'NA',rev:120000},{region:'EU',rev:98000}];return <BarChart width={400} height={240} data={data}><XAxis dataKey='region'/><YAxis/><Bar dataKey='rev' fill='#58a6ff'/></BarChart>;} return <App/>;

tools.name: viz_update
tools.short_description: Patch metadata on a saved visualization
tools.description:
Update mutable fields on an existing snapshot: title, tags, is_public, css_source, or synergy_session_id. Only the owner may update; ownership is enforced server-side by checking owner_user_id against the JWT.

The jsx_source itself is not editable here — to change the rendered code, save a new snapshot and link it. (Future enhancement: a 'fork' tool.)

USE CASES:
1. User renames a saved viz.
2. User adds tags after seeing the gallery.
3. User toggles a viz to org-public so teammates can see it.
4. User re-links a viz to a different Synergy session.

WHEN NOT TO USE:
- Changing the JSX itself → create a new snapshot with viz_create.
- Updating render_count → use the internal bump endpoint (called by the gallery on remount).

WORKFLOW:
1. User says `rename this to Pipeline Q4 and tag it sales`.
2. AI calls viz_get(snapshot_id) to confirm ownership.
3. AI calls viz_update(snapshot_id, title=`Pipeline Q4`, tags=[`sales`,`q4`,`pipeline`]).

BEST PRACTICES:
- Always confirm ownership before attempting — non-owner updates are 403.
- Use this sparingly; prefer viz_create for new work.

ERROR HANDLING:
- snapshot_id not found or wrong owner → 404 / 403.
- Empty body → 400 'no fields to update'.

RELATED TOOLS:
- viz_create — create a new snapshot.
- viz_link_synergy / viz_unlink_synergy — manage Synergy links without editing this snapshot's other fields.

snapshot_id.description: UUID of the snapshot to patch.

tools.name: viz_save
tools.description:
Convenience alias that creates a new snapshot if snapshot_id is omitted, or updates the title of an existing one if snapshot_id is supplied. Use this when the user says 'save this' without caring about whether it already exists — if a snapshot with the same title already exists in the user's library, the backend will update it; otherwise it will insert.

NOTE: V1 implementation always performs an insert when snapshot_id is absent (the gallery dedupes by title client-side and surfaces the right id to the user). The title-dedupe behaviour is a planned V2 enhancement.

USE CASES:
- Quick 'save this as <name>' without first asking the AI to look up an existing id.
- Toolbar Save button: always call viz_save so the click is safe to repeat.

WHEN NOT TO USE:
- Updating many fields at once → prefer viz_create + viz_update.
- The user wants to link to Synergy → follow up with viz_link_synergy.

RELATED TOOLS:
- viz_create / viz_update — explicit create or update.
- viz_link_synergy — link to Synergy session.

snapshot_id.description: If supplied, the title is updated on this existing snapshot instead of inserting.

tools.name: viz_search
tools.short_description: List or search saved visualizations for the calling user/org
tools.description:
Browse the visualization library. Returns a JSON array of summaries (NO jsx_source, NO thumbnail_png — those are heavy). Default scope is the calling user's own snapshots; pass synergy_session_id to filter to a single Kanban session, or pass is_public=true via a separate viz_get call to view public snapshots.

Filters can be combined:
  * q — case-insensitive ILIKE on title.
  * tag — exact match against the tags array.
  * mine=true — explicit; default already true.
  * synergy_session_id — TEXT not UUID; the synergy session_id is a slug.
  * limit / offset — pagination (default 20 / 0).

USE CASES:
1. User asks 'show my saved dashboards'.
2. User asks 'find my finance charts'.
3. AI wants to check if a similar viz already exists before creating a duplicate.
4. AI wants to enumerate snapshots linked to a Synergy session before unlinking one.

WHEN NOT TO USE:
- Need the actual JSX → call viz_get on the chosen snapshot.
- Need notes on a snapshot → call viz_list_notes.

WORKFLOW:
1. AI calls viz_search(q='pipeline') to find candidates.
2. AI surfaces 3-5 results to the user.
3. User picks one; AI calls viz_get(snapshot_id) for the full payload.

BEST PRACTICES:
- Always paginate; do not ask for >50 results in one call.
- Combine q + tag for precision (e.g. q='forecast' tag='finance').
- For Synergy linkage: viz_search(synergy_session_id='quarterly-review') returns the linked viz array.

ERROR HANDLING:
- Empty result set → return success:true with items:[].
- Invalid limit (>100) → 400.

RELATED TOOLS:
- viz_get — fetch full payload for one snapshot.
- viz_delete — soft-delete a snapshot.
- viz_link_synergy — link one of the returned snapshots.

mine.description: If true (default), only return snapshots owned by the caller. If false, return all org-visible snapshots.

synergy_session_id.description: Filter to snapshots linked to this Synergy session_id (TEXT slug).

examples.description: Snapshots linked to a Synergy session

tools.name: viz_get
tools.short_description: Fetch the full payload of one saved visualization
tools.description:
Returns a single snapshot by id. Includes jsx_source, css_source, and a base64-encoded thumbnail_png (if previously uploaded). Ownership / org-visibility check is enforced: non-owners see a redacted row (title + tags + summary only, NO jsx_source and NO thumbnail_png) unless the snapshot is_public=true.

USE CASES:
1. AI needs to re-render a snapshot (loads jsx_source into a fresh iframe).
2. AI needs to copy/clone a snapshot's JSX.
3. Gallery tile click triggers a viz_get to populate the modal.

WHEN NOT TO USE:
- Listing multiple snapshots → use viz_search.
- Need conversation provenance → call viz_get_thread afterwards.

BEST PRACTICES:
- Cache viz_get results per snapshot_id for the session — the JSX is immutable until the user creates a new snapshot.

ERROR HANDLING:
- snapshot_id not found → 404.
- Not owner and not public → 403 (returns redacted summary).

RELATED TOOLS:
- viz_search — find the snapshot id first.
- viz_read_thread — get conversation context for the snapshot.

snapshot_id.description: UUID of the snapshot to fetch.

include_payload.description: Force-include jsx_source even for non-owners (requires admin role; defaults to false).

returns.description: {success, snapshot: {id, title, jsx_source?, css_source?, tags, uses_lucide, uses_recharts, uses_tailwind, is_public, synergy_session_id, owner_user_id, thread_id, assistant_message_id, thumbnail_png?, created_at, updated_at}}

tools.name: viz_delete
tools.description:
Marks a snapshot is_active=false. The row is hidden from viz_search by default but is preserved for audit / undelete (re-activate via viz_update setting is_active implicitly through a future endpoint — V1 only supports soft-delete, no undelete).

Ownership enforced server-side: only the original owner can soft-delete.

USE CASES:
1. User says 'delete that chart'.
2. Cleaning up a test snapshot during development.

WHEN NOT TO USE:
- Hard delete → not supported in V1 (preserves audit trail).
- Undelete → not supported in V1.

WORKFLOW:
1. AI calls viz_search to confirm the snapshot id and ownership.
2. AI confirms with user: 'Delete "<title>"?' (soft-delete).
3. AI calls viz_delete(snapshot_id).

ERROR HANDLING:
- Not owner → 403.
- Already deleted → still returns success:true (idempotent).

RELATED TOOLS:
- viz_update — for metadata edits instead of deletion.

snapshot_id.description: UUID of the snapshot to delete.

tools.name: viz_get_thread
tools.short_description: Get the thread context (title + last few messages) for a saved viz
tools.description:
Given a snapshot_id, return the originating thread's metadata (title, slug, id) plus the last 4-6 messages as a short context block. Use this when an AI agent wants to 'remember' what the user was asking for when the viz was built — useful for handoff between agents.

Internally this calls viz_get to discover the thread_id, then calls /api/threads/<thread_id>/load for thread metadata and /api/threads/messages/get?thread_id=...&limit=6 for the recent messages.

USE CASES:
1. AI starts a fresh session and reads: 'What was this chart about?' — viz_get_thread gives the 6 most recent messages so it can answer.
2. Hand-off doc: a new agent reads the previous agent's handoff note (via viz_list_notes) AND the originating thread to understand the full context.

WHEN NOT TO USE:
- Need full thread transcript → use viz_read_thread.
- Snapshot has no thread_id (saved outside a chat) → returns success:true with thread:null.

BEST PRACTICES:
- Use limit=4-6 messages; full transcripts belong in viz_read_thread.
- Truncate individual message content to 400 chars to keep the response compact.

RELATED TOOLS:
- viz_read_thread — full transcript.
- viz_list_notes — AI handoff notes from previous agents.

snapshot_id.description: UUID of the snapshot whose thread context is requested.

message_limit.description: Number of recent messages to include (default 6, max 20).

returns.description: {success, snapshot_id, thread: {id, title, slug}|null, messages: [{role, content_preview, created_at}]}

tools.name: viz_read_thread
tools.short_description: Read the full message transcript of the thread that produced a saved viz
tools.description:
Returns the raw conversation (role + content + tool_calls) of the thread that produced the snapshot. Use this for deep handoff context — e.g. when a new agent needs to understand the full requirements the user gave the previous agent.

Unlike viz_get_thread, this returns the full message bodies (truncated to a configurable max_chars per message to keep payloads sane).

USE CASES:
1. 'Read what I told the previous AI about this chart.'
2. Agent A builds a forecast, agent B (next session) needs to verify the assumptions.
3. Building a 'data lineage' view: viz → thread → notes → Synergy.

WHEN NOT TO USE:
- Just need a summary → use viz_get_thread.
- Need only AI-authored handoff notes → use viz_list_notes.

BEST PRACTICES:
- Default max_chars=2000 per message; raise to 8000 only when really needed.
- Strip tool_calls metadata unless the next agent needs to reproduce the tool sequence.

RELATED TOOLS:
- viz_get_thread — short summary only.
- viz_list_notes — AI-authored notes on the snapshot itself.

snapshot_id.description: UUID of the snapshot whose thread transcript is requested.

max_chars_per_message.description: Truncate each message body to this many characters (default 2000).

include_tool_calls.description: Include tool_calls metadata in the response. Default false to keep payload small.

returns.description: {success, snapshot_id, thread_id, messages: [{id, role, content, tool_calls?, created_at}], truncated: bool}

tools.name: viz_add_note
tools.short_description: Add a note to a saved viz (human or AI authored)
tools.description:
Attach a free-form note to a snapshot. Notes have 4 kinds:
  * 'comment' — general remark (default).
  * 'todo' — flagged for follow-up; gallery shows a yellow dot.
  * 'handoff' — written by an AI agent to the NEXT AI agent that touches this viz.
  * 'data_update' — the underlying data has changed; re-render needed.

And 2 author_kinds:
  * 'human' (default) — written by a user via the gallery UI.
  * 'ai' — written by an AI agent (must supply author_agent_id, e.g. 'prime' or 'alpha-3').

USE CASES:
1. AI finishes a viz and adds a handoff note: 'This chart assumes Q3 data as of 2026-07-15. Re-fetch before re-rendering.'
2. User clicks the '+' next to a gallery tile and types a todo.
3. AI detects stale data and posts a data_update note so the user knows to re-render.

WHEN NOT TO USE:
- Notes are append-only; to 'edit' a note, add a follow-up note with a 'supersedes' reference in metadata.

BEST PRACTICES:
- Keep handoff notes short and structured: assumptions, sources, caveats.
- Set metadata for machine-readable keys, e.g. {"re_fetch_endpoint": "/api/orders?since=..."}.

ERROR HANDLING:
- Invalid note_kind or author_kind → 400.
- Not org-visible → 403.

RELATED TOOLS:
- viz_list_notes — read all notes on a snapshot (do this first in a new agent session).
- viz_read_thread — read the originating conversation.

snapshot_id.description: UUID of the snapshot to attach the note to.

note.description: The note body. Plain text; newlines preserved.

author_agent_id.description: Required when author_kind='ai'. The agent identifier (e.g. 'prime', 'alpha-1').

metadata.description: Arbitrary JSON metadata. Use for machine-readable keys (endpoints, version pins, etc.).

parameters.note: This chart uses Q3 data as of 2026-07-15. Before re-rendering, call /api/orders?since=2026-10-01 to refresh.
Update with Nov numbers before QBR.

tools.name: viz_list_notes
tools.short_description: List all notes on a saved viz (read prior agent notes before engaging)
tools.description:
Returns all notes for a snapshot ordered by created_at ASC (oldest first — matches the natural reading order for handoff). The response is paginated; the default limit covers most snapshots entirely.

USE CASES:
1. AI starts a new session on a snapshot — read prior handoff notes BEFORE re-rendering.
2. Gallery UI: render the notes side-panel when a tile is clicked.
3. Audit: list every AI-authored note for compliance review.

WHEN NOT TO USE:
- Originating conversation → use viz_read_thread.
- Just metadata → use viz_get.

BEST PRACTICES:
- Always call this first when re-engaging a snapshot — agents often leave important caveats in handoff notes.
- Filter to author_kind='ai' mentally to surface what previous agents thought.

RELATED TOOLS:
- viz_add_note — append a note.
- viz_read_thread — originating chat transcript.

author_kind_filter.description: Optional: only return notes of this author_kind.

note_kind_filter.description: Optional: only return notes of this note_kind.

returns.description: {success, snapshot_id, items: [{id, author_kind, author_agent_id?, note, note_kind, metadata, created_at}], count, has_more}

tools.name: viz_link_synergy
tools.short_description: Attach a saved viz to a Synergy Kanban session (two-sided, atomic)
tools.description:
Link a snapshot to a Synergy Kanban session. The backend runs a single PL/pgSQL helper (sessions.link_viz_to_synergy) that updates BOTH sides atomically:
  * sessions.viz_snapshots.synergy_session_id is set to the new value.
  * synergy_sessions.synergy_sessions.linked_viz_snapshots is appended with {snapshot_id, linked_at}.

This is a transactional operation — there is no partial-failure mode where one side updates and the other doesn't.

USE CASES:
1. AI attaches the 'Q3 Forecast' chart to the 'Quarterly Review' Synergy board so reviewers see it as a reference card.
2. AI re-links a snapshot from one Synergy session to another.

WHEN NOT TO USE:
- To detach → use viz_unlink_synergy (inverse).
- To create a snapshot AND link it in one step → use viz_create with synergy_session_id or viz_save.

BEST PRACTICES:
- Confirm with the user which Synergy session to link to (the session_id is a slug, not a display name).
- A snapshot can only be linked to ONE Synergy session at a time; re-linking replaces the previous link.

ERROR HANDLING:
- Synergy session_id not found → 404 (the helper returns success:false in its JSONB).
- Viz not visible to caller → 403.

RELATED TOOLS:
- viz_unlink_synergy — detach.
- viz_search(synergy_session_id=...) — list current links.

snapshot_id.description: UUID of the snapshot to link.

synergy_session_id.description: Synergy session_id (TEXT slug) to attach to. Obtained from the Synergy UI or viz_search.

label.description: Optional display label for the linked card in Synergy (e.g. 'Q3 forecast chart').

tools.name: viz_unlink_synergy
tools.short_description: Detach a saved viz from its Synergy Kanban session
tools.description:
Inverse of viz_link_synergy. Runs the PL/pgSQL helper sessions.unlink_viz_from_synergy which clears viz_snapshots.synergy_session_id AND removes the snapshot's entry from synergy_sessions.synergy_sessions.linked_viz_snapshots — atomically.

If the snapshot is not currently linked, the helper returns success:true with note='already_unlinked' (idempotent).

USE CASES:
1. User moves a chart off a Synergy board.
2. AI re-organizes: detach from old Synergy, re-attach via viz_link_synergy.

WHEN NOT TO USE:
- To re-link → call viz_link_synergy (no need to unlink first).

RELATED TOOLS:
- viz_link_synergy — link.
- viz_search(synergy_session_id=...) — list snapshots on a board.

snapshot_id.description: UUID of the snapshot to detach.
